notes: Same parts as step 1; none added or dropped.
Two separate circuits (sender with pushbutton, receiver with LED), so no repeats are used.
The catalogue card for arduino-mkr-wan-1300 has no digital pin ports. Pin 2 is used as port '2', as in the diagrams and sketches, even though the card does not list it.
The antenna's attachment point is not a port on the MKR card. The antenna is joined to the board with no port named, and not given an electrical edge.

Breadboard hole letters follow the catalogue naming (top half = bank 't', rows a-e). The image rows f, g and h on the top half are mapped to e, d and c. Only the column strip matters, since each strip is one node.

Sender: pin 2 wire at column 7 and GND wire at column 5. The pushbutton legs are in the same columns, so pressing connects pin 2 to GND. The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so no external resistor is needed.
Pushbutton: only two legs are visible in the image. They are assigned to opposite sides, 1.l at column 5 and 2.l at column 7.

Receiver: GND wire at column 6 joins the LED cathode. The LED anode is at column 8, which is the bent leg in the image. The 220 ohm resistor runs from column 8 to column 11. The pin 2 wire is in column 11. The path is pin 2, resistor, LED anode, LED cathode, GND.
The resistor value is not stated in the manual, so 220 ohm is assumed.
USB cables are joined to each board's USB port. Their computer ends are not modelled.
